articles.title: Nepal floods: How recent reports warned of this disaster months ago
articles.description: Recent floods in Nepal and Tibet followed ICIMOD's warnings about melting glaciers.  These reports highlighted doubled ice loss rates and increased flood risks across the region.  A catastrophic flash flood triggered by a glacier collapse killed hundreds and left many missing.  Smaller glaciers are shrinking faster, intensifying hazards like glacial lake outburst floods.  Regional cooperation is vital for understanding and preparing for these cross-border mountain disasters.

Relocated turtle nests produced fewer hatchlings, smaller young and a heavily female-biased sex ratio
articles.description: Relocating vulnerable sea turtle nests can lead to unexpected negative consequences. When nests are moved to warmer areas, the sex ratio of hatchlings skews heavily towards females. Additionally, even nests placed in shaded locations yield smaller hatchlings with reduced physical capabilities. Therefore, effective nest relocation must consider various environmental factors beyond just temperature to ensure the successful recovery of turtle populations.

articles.title: Sensex opens 200 points higher, Nifty hovers around 24,000 ahead of Fed chair’s address
articles.full_text: Brent crude oil prices eased 0.36% but remained elevated at around $88 per barrel, keeping energy costs and inflation concerns on investors' radar. Gold was trading at Rs 1,59,400 per 10 grams for 24-carat gold, while silver surged to Rs 2,43,366 per kg. The rupee traded around 95.401 against the US dollar after recovering from an intraday low of 95.55. Investors are now focused on comments from US Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole Symposium for clues about the outlook for inflation and global interest rates. His remarks could influence expectations around the future path of US monetary policy and consequently affect both global and Indian markets. The Nifty FMCG index declined 0.68%, while Nifty Consumer Durables fell 0.53%. Nifty Realty dropped 0.44%, Nifty Auto slipped 0.27% and Nifty Private Bank declined 0.14%. Asian markets largely ended higher, offering additional support to Indian equities. Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.27%, Singapore's Straits Times rose 0.28% and Taiwan's weighted index advanced 0.77%. South Korea's KOSPI, however, fell 1.82%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng slipped 0.01%. Indian equity markets ended higher on Friday, led by a strong rally in IT stocks as investors tracked gains in global technology shares and renewed optimism over artificial intelligence spending. The Nifty 50 gained 84.80 points, or 0.35%, to close at 24,175.65, while the BSE Sensex rose 330.92 points, or 0.43%, to end at 77,264.51. The Nifty IT index emerged as the day's biggest sectoral gainer, rising more than 3%. The rally followed an overnight surge in US technology stocks after Nvidia reported strong second-quarter results and issued an upbeat revenue outlook, boosting expectations for continued global investment in AI. TCS, Tech Mahindra, Infosys, Wipro and HCL Technologies were among the biggest Nifty 50 gainers, along with Bajaj Auto. Gains in technology stocks helped offset weakness across several other sectors. "Investors are awaiting further clarity on geopolitical developments. Domestic equities ended largely flat. The Nifty IT index emerged as the top gainer, rising over 3%, tracking the overnight rally in US technology stocks and recovering from the recent selloff," said Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services. Tempsens Instruments specialises in thermal engineering products, temperature-sensing equipment, electrical heating solutions and specialised cables. The company plans to use Rs 73.13 crore from the fresh issue to support its expansion and strengthen its finances. Of this, Rs 18.13 crore will go towards capital expenditure for its electrical heating and specialised cable businesses, while Rs 55 crore will be used for prepayment or scheduled repayment of outstanding borrowings. The remaining funds will be used for general corporate purposes. SBI securities head of fundamental research Sunny Agrawal said Tempsens Instruments had strong positions in temperature sensing, specialised cables and electrical heating solutions. He said the company was India's largest temperature sensor manufacturer, with a 10.5% market share, while it held a 21.3% share in non-contact temperature sensors. The company also recorded strong financial growth between FY24 and FY26, with revenue, EBITDA and profit after tax growing at compound annual growth rates of 27.2%, 35.2% and 28.2%, respectively. Exports accounted for 28.5% of FY26 revenue, highlighting its expanding international presence. Agrawal also pointed to high entry barriers created by stringent certifications, lengthy customer qualification processes, specialised engineering expertise and established relationships with mission-critical industries. For investors who received IPO allotments, he recommended holding the stock from a long-term perspective, depending on their risk profile. Investors who were targeting only the listing gains could book profits, while those seeking a fresh entry should consider buying on dips rather than chasing the stock after its sharp debut. “For investors who have received an IPO allotment, we would recommend holding on to the stock from a long-term perspective, subject to their individual risk profile. Those who have applied only for listing pop can book profit. Investors looking for a fresh entry may consider following a “Buy on Dips” strategy, rather than chasing the stock at elevated levels,” Agrawal said. Shares of Tempsens Instruments made a blockbuster debut on Friday, more than doubling investors' money by listing at a 111% premium over its issue price. The stock opened at Rs 634 apiece on the NSE, compared with its IPO price of Rs 300. It gained marginally to Rs 634.85 before falling more than 8% to an intraday low of Rs 582. Despite the decline, the stock remained around 94% above its issue price. The strong debut followed intense investor interest in the company's Rs 650-crore initial public offering, which was subscribed 184 times during its three-day bidding period. The IPO comprised a fresh issue of Rs 95 crore and an offer for sale worth Rs 555 crore. Before the issue opened, Tempsens Instruments also raised Rs 194.54 crore from anchor investors. SEBI issued the consultation paper on August 27 and has invited public comments on the draft circular until September 17. If finalised, the proposed provisions would come into effect "with immediate effect", according to the draft circular. All other provisions under Chapter V of the Non-Convertible Securities (NCS) Master Circular would remain unchanged. Under the draft framework, the debt securities covered by the exemption would have to meet additional safeguards aimed at limiting the provision to relatively lower-risk instruments. The securities would have to be unsubordinated or senior and secured by a first or pari passu charge over identifiable assets of the issuer. They would also need to carry a minimum AA- rating on the date of the private placement. SEBI said the conditions were intended to ensure that the exemption applied only to instruments with relatively lower risk. The regulator said the proposal was also based on the view that "sufficient information about the issuer is already available in public domain", given that listed companies are subject to regulatory oversight and disclosure requirements. The issuer would have to be registered with or regulated by a financial-sector regulator in India and listed on a recognised stock exchange for at least one year. At the time of granting in-principle approval, the stock exchange would also have to confirm that there were no pending SEBI or exchange fines or penalties relating to applicable LODR compliance. The issuer must also have recorded no defaults during the previous three financial years or the current financial year on specified obligations, including repayments linked to debt securities, deposits, dividends and term loans. It would also have to submit an auditor's certificate to the stock exchange. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed exempting certain listed issuers from the mandatory appointment of a merchant banker when raising small-value debt through private placement, citing high costs, limited availability of merchant bankers and delays in execution. Under the proposal, the exemption would cover debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares issued through private placement with a face value of Rs 10,000, subject to specified eligibility conditions. SEBI said market participants had raised concerns over the burden associated with appointing merchant bankers for such offerings. The consultation paper highlighted the "Disproportionate burden of the appointment cost", along with the limited number of merchant bankers operating in the debt segment and delays that could affect fundraising. The quity markets opened higher after two consecutive sessions of losses, although investor caution remained ahead of a speech by Federal Reserve Chair and following sharp swings during the previous session's closing auction. The Nifty 50 rose 0.13% to 24,122.60, while the BSE Sensex gained 0.25% to 77,128.05 at 9.15am IST. Thirteen of the 16 major sectoral indices advanced in early trade. The broader market also opened firmer, with the small-cap and mid-cap indices rising 0.2% and 0.1%, respectively. The benchmarks had fallen around 1% each over the previous two sessions and were on course for a third consecutive weekly decline. Elevated oil prices and higher US Treasury yields continued to weigh on global risk appetite. Investor sentiment was also affected by Thursday's volatile closing auction, which coincided with the monthly derivatives expiry. Derivatives turnover on the BSE index was at its lowest level in 11 months for a monthly expiry session. The indicative Sensex close briefly fell more than 3% during the closing auction before recovering some of the losses and eventually ending 0.7% lower. Markets were therefore expected to remain volatile, with investors closely watching the Federal Reserve chair's remarks for clues on the US interest-rate outlook.
